short: The flagship of the Russian Black Sea Fleet, famously sunk during the 2022 invasion of Ukraine.
full:
Commissioned on 30 January 1983 as Slava ("Glory"), this guided missile cruiser was later renamed Moskva and served as the flagship of the Russian Black Sea Fleet. Designed as a heavily armed surface combatant during the late Cold War, its primary offensive armament consisted of sixteen massive P-1000 Vulkan anti-ship cruise missiles. For decades, it projected Soviet and later Russian naval power in the Mediterranean and the Black Sea.

Moskva gained international infamy during the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine when it was involved in the capture of Snake Island. On 14 April 2022, the ship suffered catastrophic damage and sank after being struck by two Ukrainian Neptune anti-ship missiles. Its destruction marked the largest warship sunk in combat since the Falklands War and represented a profound symbolic and strategic victory for Ukraine, severely degrading Russian naval dominance in the region.
